sb_prompt: WHAT ADVICE OR EXPERIENCE CAN YOU OFFER TO A PARENT ON HOW TO HELP A SON OR DAUGHTER CHOOSE A COLLEGE TO ATTEND?
turns: Yeah, I'm glad you called because honestly, picking a school was a total mess for me too, especially since my buddy from back in the day ended up in a program he hated and it really shook up my whole idea of what actually matters.

Yeah, man, that is exactly why I never want my kid to go somewhere just because it's popular. I remember when my daughter was in high school, she got into this fancy private college everyone talked about, but she hated every minute of it. She came home crying so much I thought she'd drop out, and honestly, it took her two years to find a community where she actually felt like she belonged.
That is so rough though, did she end up finding somewhere she loves now?

Yeah, she actually transferred to a public school nearby last fall, and she's been so happy since, mostly because the professors actually know her name and she can just walk into the lounge after class.

That's actually huge for her, honestly, because looking back, I probably would have stayed in that fancy place just to save some money for my own loans, even though I knew deep down I wouldn't have fit in.
Yeah, I totally get that, but honestly I think the fancy name was the only thing that mattered to your parents, so it's tough to explain to them that a smaller school is better.
Yeah, that's the hardest part because you can't convince them that their reputation doesn't actually translate to your happiness.

Yeah, honestly, when my own kids look at lists, they just see the ranking number and want the top one, and I keep telling them to ignore the brand and look at the vibe because a small college can actually change your life more than a big name ever could.

Yeah, you're totally right about the vibe, because I actually know this guy who went to a super prestigious place just to please his parents and ended up miserable, so I've been telling my younger brother to look for somewhere where he actually feels comfortable instead of chasing that number.
Yeah, that's the scary part, because once you see your kid struggling in a classroom where no one knows who they are, it's way harder to get them to come home and tell you the truth.

Yeah, and honestly, if I had just stayed at that school for the parents, I'd probably be stuck there forever just working menial jobs while everyone else moved on, but luckily my brother is finally looking at trade schools and community colleges instead.
That's a good plan, but I'm worried he'll still try to push for the big name just to make us look good.

Yeah, that's exactly why I'm trying to tell him to look at the club fliers and the student photos instead of the brochure, because if he can't see himself there, the fancy degree is just a piece of paper that doesn't mean anything.

Yeah, tell him to go look at the actual student photos in the library rather than the glossy brochure, because if he can't see himself hanging out with those kids, the degree is just a piece of paper.

Yeah, tell him to skip the glossy stuff and just go hang out in the student union for an afternoon, because if he doesn't feel like he belongs there by noon, he shouldn't sign up even if it's ranked number one.
Yeah, that's the truth—once he walks in and realizes the vibe isn't right, he'll probably just leave and find something real.
Yeah, that's the thing, you can't just look at the stats, you gotta actually sit in the cafeteria and see if you'd feel out of place.
Yeah, that's the only way to really tell if it's gonna work out.
Yeah, and if he's feeling awkward after the first hour, he should just keep his eyes open for a smaller program where people actually talk to each other instead of just staring at screens.
Yeah, that's the only way to know if it's actually going to work.
Yeah, and honestly if he keeps finding it too stiff, I think he should just look for places where the classes are smaller and the professors actually teach instead of just lecturing.
Yeah, small classes are better because then you actually get to talk to the teacher instead of just watching them talk at everyone else.
Yeah, that's exactly what I'm telling him, stop watching the slides and actually ask the prof a question during office hours.
Yeah, but honestly sometimes the classes are just small because the school can't afford to hire enough people to keep it going, so you gotta make sure they actually care about teaching.
Right, but you gotta check if the teaching actually happens or if they just hired the same adjuncts for a decade because the big-name school can't pay full-time professors.

Yeah, that's the tricky part, because at a big school you can always blame the adjunct on the system, but at a small place you have to actually fight to get a good teacher since everyone else is on the same boat.
Yeah, but at least if it's a small school, when you mess up, the whole town notices and the prof actually talks to you about fixing it instead of just letting you fail silently.
Yeah, that's exactly why I tell my kids to visit the library first because if the professors aren't there to help you fix it, there's no one to turn to.
Yeah, I guess if you're at a tiny place, you're stuck with everyone knowing your business, but at least someone is actually paying attention when you need help.
Yeah, that's the scary part about small towns, everyone knows your GPA and if you don't do well, you're stuck there forever.
Yeah, but I guess the trade-off is that at a small school you can't hide your mistakes, which is terrifying if you're just starting out.
Yeah, that's the risk, but I'd rather they make a mistake and learn than never really know where they stand.
Yeah, but sometimes knowing everyone watching you feel like you're gonna get crushed if you mess up.
Yeah, but maybe the pressure of everyone watching is exactly what keeps you honest when you're figuring things out for the first time.
Yeah, but honestly, that kind of pressure might make him quit before he even starts if he's not sure if he wants it.
Yeah, I guess that pressure is better than just drifting through a giant campus without anyone caring if you're actually trying.
Yeah, but if he's too scared to try, then the whole point of going to college is just lost on him.
Yeah, maybe he'll finally realize that being forced to perform isn't the same as actually learning.
Yeah, but honestly if he feels crushed before he even gets there, then maybe he shouldn't force himself into a place where he's already failing.
Yeah, that's the scary part, because once he realizes he can't fake it, he might just bail before the first semester even starts.
